html:
The Kingdom of Kandy was the hill kingdom of central Sri Lanka from 1469 to 1815, the last independent Sinhalese state. It began as a breakaway from the Kingdom of Kotte. Its mountains and forests made it hard to invade, and it outlasted three European powers on the coast.

  • The Portuguese invaded several times in the late 1500s and early 1600s and were beaten back (Portuguese Ceylon).
  • King Rajasinghe II allied with the Dutch in 1638 to expel the Portuguese. The Dutch then kept the coast for themselves (Dutch Ceylon), cutting Kandy off from the sea.
  • From 1739 its kings came from the Nayak family of Madurai in south India. They were patrons of Buddhism.

The kings kept the Tooth Relic of the Buddha in the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy city, the sign of their right to rule. In 1815 Kandyan nobles turned against the last king, Sri Vikrama Rajasinha, and helped the British depose him. The Kandyan Convention made the kingdom part of British Ceylon. A large revolt in 1817 and 1818 was put down hard.
